Svalbard has a separate Norwegian tax system, administered by Skatteetaten, using NOK and the calendar year. Gross salary withholding and separately assessed ordinary income are distinct. The eight Guides are **source-cited drafts**, not accountant-reviewed. The six previously reviewed Guides are preserved; the two additional levy Guides received [independent AI review on 31 October 2026](../../evidence/ledgers/svalbard-finish-20261031/independent-review/final-report.md), with their explicit limits retained. The three explicit domain gaps above and the additional job limits below keep issue #424 open.

Ordinary scope includes residents/nonresidents, employment/pensions, sole traders, capital income and wealth, company profit and allocation, depreciation/losses, membership and contribution classes, employer withholding, standard benefits, related-party pricing/documentation, residence/departure and foreign distributions. Guide presence and passing arithmetic are not proof of full coverage.
## Additional tax jobs and territorial exclusions
The seven-domain coverage report does not inventory every statutory levy. The full-country goal also requires the following jobs and their operational limits to be accounted for.
| Job | Guide or official basis | Current status |

| Visitor environmental levy, collection and resident refund | [sj-svalbard-visitor-environmental-levy](sj-svalbard-visitor-environmental-levy.md) | Ordinary charge and published refund procedure drafted with a figure ledger. Carrier settlement/remittance, incorporated aviation exceptions and post-access refund-form fields remain unverified. |

| Coal-export duty | [sj-svalbard-coal-export-duty](sj-svalbard-coal-export-duty.md) | Enacted 2026 bands, seasonal FOB method and statutory book/assessment/payment/appeal rules drafted with a figure ledger. Current departmental filing format/channel and coal-specific interest rate remain unverified; the last listed band is not extrapolated. |

| Document transfer duty on Svalbard property | [Kartverket's Svalbard exclusion under Svalbard Act §2](https://www.kartverket.no/eiendom/dokumentavgift-og-gebyr/fritak-for-dokumentavgift), read 2026-10-31 | Does not apply to Svalbard property transfers. Registration fees are a separate charge and are not described as a document transfer tax. |

| Import customs duty into Svalbard | [Customs Duty Act §1-1(2)](https://lovdata.no/dokument/NL/lov/2022-03-11-8) and [Tolletaten's current Svalbard guidance](https://www.toll.no/no/bedrift/import/tolletaten-pa-svalbard/), read 2026-10-31 | Svalbard is outside the Act's customs-duty territory. Customs controls and destination-territory import duties remain separate obligations. |

This map is not a claim that every special charge has been exhausted. Financial/minimum-tax perimeter, other mineral charging decisions, special group settlements, regulated-sector charges and the current local fee schedules still need a positive applicability/job audit. The existing specialist exclusions below describe what the original six Guides supply; they do not remove applicable jobs from the full-country goal. The new coal-export Guide supplies a tax job that was not covered by the original extractive-sector exclusion.

Niche exclusions: simplified settlements for foreign research/project groups and Barentsburg; offshore/extractive and shipping regimes; financial institutions; large-multinational minimum tax and Svalbard-specific CbC perimeter implementation; reorganisations and complex hybrid arrangements; specialist pensions/benefits; short-term accommodation; and treaty-rate tables. These do not erase the ordinary gaps declared above. Professional sign-off is a separate trust limit, not a `partial` reason.
